error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the relay at that URL.

abort.already_configured: This relay is already set up.

stale_telemetry.title: Water heater data is stale
stale_telemetry.description: **{heater}**: The iCOMM relay is running, but the tank has not reported for {age} minutes (LAN session: {lan}; relay health: {health}). The water heater shows its last-known values and writes are still accepted and queued. If this persists, check the relay's Pending write and Relay health sensors, or power-cycle the water heater's breaker.

confirm.title: Allow the {target} firmware update?
confirm.description:
Ayla offered firmware {version} ({size}, from {host}) for the {target}. The relay is holding it, so the heater keeps running the firmware it has (Wi-Fi module: {agent}).

**Installing it could end local control.** This integration works because the current module firmware accepts the relay in place of Ayla's cloud. An update that checks certificates would cut the relay out, and the heater would go offline until the router steering is removed.

Submit to let this one update through on the module's next poll. To keep it held, close this and choose Ignore.

abort.not_loaded: The iCOMM integration isn't loaded; reload it and try again.
abort.relay_refused: The relay no longer has this update on hold (Ayla may have withdrawn it). Nothing was changed.

upstream_certificate.title: The iCOMM relay can't verify Ayla's cloud
upstream_certificate.description:
The relay refused Ayla's TLS certificate ({error}). That has happened {failures} times; Ayla last verified {since}. Until it's resolved, the heater's data no longer reaches Ayla, so the A.O. Smith app goes stale and app commands stop. Local control through Home Assistant still works.

Most likely Ayla moved to a certificate that no longer chains to the root the relay trusts (Entrust Root G2). Update the iCOMM Local Relay add-on, or report it at {issues_url}. The other possibility is something between your network and Ayla presenting its own certificate, which is exactly what this check is for.

telemetry_frozen.title: Water heater data is frozen
telemetry_frozen.description:
**{heater}**: The water heater keeps reporting, but every report for the last {minutes} minutes has been identical.{power} The controller's live reporting has lapsed, which happens some hours after the A.O. Smith app was last opened and after a reboot, so the temperatures, power and hot-water figures in Home Assistant may be wrong. Heating itself isn't affected.

{fix} This warning clears by itself once the data changes again.

dns_server_failed.title: The iCOMM relay's DNS steering isn't working
dns_server_failed.description:
The relay add-on's `dns_server` option is on, but {problem}. Until that's fixed, the water heater can't reach the relay through DNS, and local control stops at its next reboot.

Usually another add-on owns the port: a DNS server such as AdGuard or Pi-hole (port 53), or an SSL proxy such as NGINX (port 443). Either stop that add-on, or turn `dns_server` off and use that add-on instead (for AdGuard, add a DNS rewrite for the water heater's name).

cloud_idle.title: Water heater isn't reaching Ayla
cloud_idle.description:
**{heater}**: Local Connect is working, so Home Assistant has live data and control, but the water heater hasn't contacted Ayla's cloud for {minutes} minutes. The A.O. Smith app won't show current data, and app changes won't reach the heater. This can follow a relay restart or a reboot of the Home Assistant host: the heater's Wi-Fi module gives up on the cloud after a failed connection and doesn't retry while Local Connect works.

To fix it, flip the water heater's breaker off for about 30 seconds, then on. It signs in to Ayla again within a minute; nothing is lost. This warning clears by itself once it does.

init.title: Optional power sensor
init.description: A power sensor on the water heater's own circuit (for example an Emporia or smart-plug channel). It lets Home Assistant spot frozen water heater data sooner: unchanged for 30 minutes while this sensor shows the heater running.
